findings.title: The new type-only exemption is applied to the wildcard path only: a type-only NAMED re-export of a handler verb is still reported as an ungated handler, and the namespace form's message asserts a reachability that cannot exist
findings.reason: Measured by calling the shipped `scanRouteFile` directly at HEAD (no mutation): `export type { GET } from './types'` and `export { type GET } from './types'` in an otherwise-clean admin route each produce "GET is re-exported from another module, so this audit cannot see its gate" — a FALSE POSITIVE in a fail-closed CI control, since a type-only re-export creates no runtime binding and Next.js routes nothing. The fix hunk states that principle itself ("`export type * from` is exempt: a type-only re-export creates no runtime binding for Next.js to route") and `export type * from` is correctly CLEAN, so the exemption is inconsistent within one commit; `readNamedExportAliases` (:424) has no `isTypeOnly` check on either the declaration or the element. Second, smaller half: `export * as ns from './handlers'` and `export * as GET from './handlers'` are reported with "Next.js routes whatever it exports, so an ungated handler would be reachable" — a namespace re-export binds exactly one name to a module-namespace OBJECT, which Next cannot route as a handler, so the finding fires correctly-conservatively but its stated consequence is not true for that form. Both are cheap to close (an isTypeOnly guard; a form-specific message). Neither is exploitable — the direction is toward a finding, never toward silence.

findings.title: A dropped `await` on the page gate survives on five of the six flipped pages — the suite's own header claims it pins that, and no other gate (ci:admin-aal2, eslint, tsc) detects it
findings.arbiter_reasoning: The mutation is semantically meaningful and NOT equivalent: `requireAdminPage` refuses by calling `redirect()`, which signals by throwing. Awaited, the throw stops the page; un-awaited, it lands in a discarded promise and the page continues into its service reads and renders data to a caller the gate refused — the parallel read path rule P2 exists to close. It is not on an unexecuted branch either: the test invokes the page's default export directly, so the mutated statement is on the path the test runs. The claim is therefore about the ORACLE, not about coverage. Control: the suite's refusal-propagation test imports only ../overview/page, and the identical mutation applied to overview WAS killed (INV-R3-M12), which is exactly why five of the six pages survived and one did not. Recorded here in its own field because the schema requires it; the round-3 agent wrote this reasoning into `reason`, where the checker could not see it.
findings.reason: FIXED at 4a588cdd, in the MOCK rather than the assertion: `mockRequireAdminPage` now awaits a `setTimeout(0)` BEFORE `callOrder.push('gate')`, so an un-awaited gate lets a service record first and `callOrder[0]` is 'read'. The FIRST attempt was itself vacuous — it added the yield to the hoisted implementation while `beforeEach` reinstalled the synchronous body before every test, and re-running the sweep still showed five survivors; the body now has one owner (`gateImplementation`) that both sites use. RE-MEASURED BY THE ROOT at 4a588cdd (root evidence gathered OUTSIDE a red-team round, and marked as such rather than presented as a mutation-runner result), dropping `await` on each of the six pages in turn and restoring after each: /admin/overview 2 failed, /admin/businesses 1 failed, /admin/businesses/[id] 1 failed, /admin/costs 1 failed, /admin/jobs 1 failed, /admin/notifications 1 failed — dead on all six, where round 3 measured five survivors. The finding's own FIX SHAPE suggestion (make the refusal test `it.each`) was not taken: fixing the mock kills the mutation on all six through the step-up test itself, rather than adding a second test that depends on the same synchronous-recording flaw. ORIGINAL FINDING: MEASURED (INV-R3-M10 / M11). `src/app/admin/costs/page.tsx`: `await requireAdminPage(...)` → `requireAdminPage(...)` (plain floating promise) and, separately, `void requireAdminPage(...)`. Under BOTH, the test `'/admin/costs' steps up to aal2 before reading anything` PASSES (baseline green, exactly one test executed each run); `pnpm ci:admin-aal2` passes (35 route files, 21 pages) because `readAdminPageGate` requires only a CallExpression; `npx eslint src/app/admin/costs/page.tsx` is clean (`@typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises` is not configured in eslint.config.mjs); `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean for that file. Line 166 pins `callOrder[0] === 'gate'`, which an un-awaited gate satisfies — the async mock's body runs synchronously to its first await, so 'gate' is pushed first while the promise is discarded. ARBITER CONFIRMATION: the mutation is semantically meaningful and NOT equivalent — `requireAdminPage` refuses by calling `redirect()`, which signals by throwing; awaited, the throw stops the page; un-awaited, it lands in a discarded promise and the page continues into getCostReport/getMarginReport and renders cross-account spend and margin to a caller the gate refused, which is exactly the parallel read path rule P2 exists to close. The mutated statement is on the path the test executes (the test invokes the page's default export directly), so it is not an unexecuted branch. This is a claim about the ORACLE. CONTROL: the suite's refusal-propagation test `a refused step-up stops the page before any data read` (line 169) imports only `../overview/page` (line 177); INV-R3-M12 applied the identical mutation to src/app/admin/overview/page.tsx and that test KILLED it — so /admin/overview is covered and /admin/{businesses,businesses/[id],costs,jobs,notifications} are not. FIX SHAPE: make the refusal test `it.each(PAGES)` the way the step-up test already is.

findings.title: Duty-4 sibling: an admin-capable handler outside the widened ROUTES contract’s path scope, which the audit cannot see by construction
findings.reason: `scanRouteFile` is path-scoped — `if (!normalized.includes('src/app/api/admin/')) return [];` (admin-aal2-audit.ts:622). src/app/api/zernio/disconnect/route.ts:69 calls `requireRole(req, 'owner', 'admin')`, so an admin acts there at plain role with no AAL2 step-up and the ROUTES contract cannot bind it. This QUALIFIES the arch-review-log's phrasing that the widening makes "every Admin API handler calls a gate this audit has vetted" a CI-enforced fact: it is a fact about src/app/api/admin/**, the correct scope for this ticket and for ADR 0025, but not the same as every handler an admin can reach. Pre-existing and unchanged by this branch; recorded as the Duty-4 result rather than raised as a new front against unchanged code. Any change belongs to its own ticket. P2 never blocks.
